# Make weapon tuning data-driven via CSV (designer-retunable without TypeScript)

## Goal

Designers can retune **fire rate, bullet colours, bullet sizes, AoE radii and impact cues** for every player weapon by editing a committed CSV (and, optionally, by saving from a gym panel) — with **no TypeScript edit** and no rebuild of source constants.

User story:

- As a **designer**, I want to open `src/data/weapons.csv`, change a weapon's fire rate, colour, bullet size, AoE radius or impact cue, refresh `npm run dev`, and see the change in the game, so I can iterate on feel without opening TypeScript or asking an engineer.
- As a **designer**, I want to adjust the same values with sliders in a gym panel and press Save, so the committed CSV is updated and the running scene reflects it immediately.
- As a **developer**, I want the shipped catalogue and the CSV to be provably identical (parity-locked by a test), so a hand edit cannot silently retune the game.

## Problem statement

Every weapon's tunables live as code in `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, 16 entries: `cannon, spread, dual, rapid, wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options, nova, mortar, arc, rear_guard, broadside, railgun, shard_swarm, heavy_slug`). The shape is already pure data — no function fields — so the catalogue is mechanically movable to a file. Retuning a fire rate, a bullet colour, a bullet size, an AoE radius or an impact cue currently requires a TypeScript edit, a code review and a build.

The repo already ships exactly the machinery needed for a different config family (`AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA`): CSV codec (`src/core/csv.ts`), boot-time registry (`src/core/configStore.ts`), bundled `?raw` imports (`src/core/bundledConfig.ts`), a dev-only atomic write API (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`), and a parity test pattern (`src/data/csv-seed.test.ts`).

## Scope (in)

- `src/data/weapons.csv` — one row per weapon, scalar columns only (fire rate / beat subdivision, colours, bullet size & lifetime, rim/thickness/trail/flame, AoE descriptor fields, orbit descriptor fields, damage/bounce/split budgets, muzzle-flash spec, impact-flash spec + cue name).
- `src/data/weapon-patterns.csv` — long format `weaponId,index,angleDeg,sideOffsetPx` for the `offsets` / `sideOffsets` angle arrays (angles authored in **degrees**, converted to radians on parse).
- `src/data/weapon-levels.json` — the per-weapon Euclidean cadence ladders (`{ k, n, rotation }` per rung), moved from `WEAPON_EUCLIDEAN_LADDER_SPECS`. **This is the live fire-rate surface** (see the fire-rate decision below); it is JSON, not CSV, because the ladders are nested per weapon per level.
- Parsed catalogue becomes the runtime source of truth, with the TS catalogue retained as the fallback for malformed/missing data (same ladder as enemy/ship CSV).
- Dev-only write path for the two new CSVs, plus a weapon tuning panel with Save / Save As and re-read.
- Runtime validation of the invariants currently enforced by types and doc-guard tests.

## Scope decision — fire rate (option (b), accepted 2026-11-03)

**Superseded:** the ladder migration was originally out of scope as follow-up AH-0MW0Q1TQV009M8AO. It is now **in scope** as a child of this epic, because the stated goal ("designers can retune fire rate without TypeScript") cannot be met by the CSV alone: the live cadence is the Euclidean ladder (`resolveWeaponPattern` → `Player._resolveFirePattern`), and `WeaponDefinition.fireRateMs` is not consulted when firing.

- **Chosen:** (b) move the ladders to `src/data/weapon-levels.json` with a code-default fallback and a frozen rung-for-rung parity fixture. Rhythms are nested per level and carry rotations/equal-density shape morphs, which a scalar CS column cannot express.
- **Rejected (a) — narrow the fire-rate claim:** would ship a designer-facing "fire rate" column that is read, validated and displayed but not heard (already wrong for six weapons: cannon 2 vs 2.25, rapid 6 vs 3.25, arc 1 vs 2.25, railgun 0.25 vs 0.5, shard_swarm 1 vs 2.5, heavy_slug 0.5 vs 0.75 onsets/beat). Rejected as the epic's headline goal.
- **Rejected (c) — derive ladder rung 0 from CSV `subdivisions`:** would create a second cadence source of truth, quantise editor input lossily to the 16th-note lattice (2.4 → 2.25/2.5), and silently re-time every upgrade threshold (they derive from `baseDensity × fireRate.cap`). It also cannot express rotations or shape morphs, so the JSON migration would still be needed afterwards.

Consequence: `subdivisions`/`fireRateMs` in `weapons.csv` stay as the **legacy nominal** value (level-stat quantisation and the hold-full ghost metronome interval). Firing cadence is authored only in `weapon-levels.json`, and a dev diagnostic flags any divergence between the two.
- Making brand-new weapons addable by CSV row alone. A new weapon still needs an icon arm (`src/powerups/icons.ts`) and an audio cue arm (`src/audio/effects.ts`); this epic makes weapons **editable**, not addable.

## Acceptance criteria (epic)

1. **Commitment.** The epic is done only when all its children (1–10, including the Euclidean ladder data migration) are closed and all tests from previous epics still pass.
2. **Single source of truth.** Runtime reads of the catalogue resolve from the parsed CSV; editing `src/data/weapons.csv` or `src/data/weapon-patterns.csv` changes the live game with no TypeScript edit. Fire **cadence** is the one exception by design and is owned by `src/data/weapon-levels.json`: editing a ladder rung changes what the weapon plays with no TypeScript edit, and the CSV `subdivisions` value is documented as the legacy nominal value only (no TypeScript edit is needed for either surface).
3. **Parity.** A frozen-fixture test proves the parsed catalogue is deep-equal to the pre-migration `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` for all 16 weapons; the migration changes no gameplay value.
4. **Validated.** Malformed rows, unknown columns, invalid enums, off-beat fire rates, duplicate colours/shapes and out-of-range numbers are rejected with a diagnostic or fall back to the code default — the game still boots.
5. **Dev-only writes.** A designer can Save / Save As from the weapon tuning panel under `npm run dev`; production/static builds stay read-only with a visible message.
6. **Documented.** CSV schema, retuning workflow, invariants and the read-only production behaviour are documented in `docs/BALANCING.md` (plus any `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` touch-point) and reflected in code comments where the catalogue is consumed.
7. **UK English** throughout, and the full suite passes (`/skill:test`), with `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` clean.

## Constraints

- **Format:** flat scalar columns; nested descriptors flattened with a stable prefix (`orbitPods`, `orbitRadius`, `aoeTrigger`, `aoeRadius`, `muzzleColor`, `impactCue`, …); colours as `0xRRGGBB`.
- **No new runtime dependency** — reuse the existing hand-rolled RFC 4180 codec.
- **No behavioural change** in the migration: `fireRateMs` stays derived from beat subdivisions (`src/utils/beat.ts`), so the on-beat-grid invariant (`isOnBeatGrid`) still holds for the whole catalogue.
- **`WEAPON_CATALOGUE` keeps its exported name and type** (`Record<WeaponId, WeaponDefinition>`) so the 16 non-test consumers (`Player.ts`, `weaponLevels.ts`, `dropLayer.ts`, `dropDescriptions.ts`, `gymHelp.ts`, `captureCycle.ts`, `GymRhythm.ts`) do not change.
- Work happens in the `implement` worktree per project policy; never edit the main checkout.

## Existing state (references)

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, `WeaponDefinition`, `BulletShape`, `OrbitDescriptor`, `AoEDescriptor`, `MuzzleFlashSpec`, `ImpactFxSpec`, `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS`, `isOnBeatGrid`, `getWeaponById`.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — `resolveWeaponDefinition(id, level)` merges level stats over a base definition; unchanged by this epic (ladders stay in code).
- `src/core/csv.ts` — RFC 4180 parser/serialiser, typed coercion, `ENEMY_COLUMN_ORDER`-style column contracts.
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — `ALLOWED_CSV_FILES`, `GET/PUT`, atomic temp+rename writes, `apply: 'serve'`.
- `src/core/bundledConfig.ts` — `?raw` bundled CSV imports.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — the committed-CSV ↔ code parity test pattern.
- `src/utils/weaponVisualRoster.docs.test.ts`, `weaponFeelRoster.test.ts`, `powerUpWeaponRosterDocs.test.ts` — invariants (unique shape family, unique colour, roster docs) that become runtime/data validation.
- Panel precedent: `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` + `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` + `src/data/bot-tuning.json` (dev panel with write-back).

## Risks

- **Silent retune on a typo.** Mitigation: frozen parity fixture + runtime validation with fallback-to-code-default.
- **Loss of compile-time exhaustiveness.** `Record<WeaponId, WeaponDefinition>` no longer proves completeness. Mitigation: explicit runtime `WEAPON_IDS` list plus a boot-time self-check test asserting every id resolves.
- **Wide CSV (≈30 columns) is intimidating to hand-edit.** Mitigation: header comment block with column docs (as `enemy-configs.csv` does), plus the tuning panel.
- **Angles in a spreadsheet.** Mitigation: degrees in the pattern CSV, radians at the boundary, documented.

# Tests: weapon catalogue CSV codec + frozen parity fixture

Test-first half of the weapons-CSV epic (parent AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7).

## Goal

Write the failing tests that define the weapon CSV contract **before** the codec exists, plus the frozen fixture that proves the CSV round-trips to the exact pre-migration catalogue.

## Deliverables

- `src/core/csv.weapons.test.ts` — tests for `parseWeaponCatalogue(csv, patternsCsv)` / `coerceWeaponRow` / `validateWeaponRow`:
  - a known-good two-row fixture parses to typed `WeaponDefinition`s with `fireRateMs` derived from the beat subdivision;
  - comment lines (`#`) and blank lines in the file are ignored;
  - colours parse from `0xRRGGBB` and reject non-hex;
  - missing optional columns (e.g. `bounce`, `splits`, `orbitPods`, `aoeTrigger`) leave the field absent rather than `0`, so presence-based dispatch (`weapon.orbit ? … : …`) still behaves;
  - invalid enum (`bulletShape`, `aoeTrigger`) is rejected with a row/column diagnostic;
  - malformed number, negative `bulletSize`, out-of-range `bulletLifetime` → validation error naming the row;

# Weapon catalogue CSV codec: parse, coerce, validate, serialise

Implementation half of the weapons-CSV epic (parent AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7).

## Goal

Extend the existing RFC 4180 codec (`src/core/csv.ts`) with a typed weapon-catalogue codec, in the same style as `coerceEnemyConfig` / `ENEMY_COLUMN_ORDER`. No new dependency; no duplicated CSV parsing logic.

## Deliverables

- `WEAPON_COLUMN_ORDER: (keyof WeaponRow)[]` — stable column contract, exported (like `ENEMY_COLUMN_ORDER`) so the Vite plugin can validate headers.
- `WeaponRow` type — the flat, scalar projection of `WeaponDefinition`:
  `id, name, description, subdivisions, bulletColor, bulletShape, bulletSize, bulletLifetime, bulletShapeLength, bulletRim, bulletThickness, bulletTrail, bulletFlame, maxHitPoints, bounce, splits, orbitPods, orbitRadius, aoeTrigger, aoeRadius, aoeDamagesEnemies, aoeClearsEnemyBullets, aoeDamage, aoeChains, aoeProjectileSpeed, hitscanLength, hitscanDuration, muzzleColor, muzzleRadius, muzzleDuration, impactColor, impactRadius, impactDuration, impactCue`
- `parseWeaponPatterns(csv)` — long format `weaponId,index,angleDeg,sideOffsetPx` → `{ offsets, sideOffsets }` per weapon; degrees → radians at the boundary.
- `coerceWeaponRow(row)` — typed coercion; **optional columns stay absent** when blank (`bounce`/`splits`/`maxHitPoints`/`bulletShapeLength`/`bulletRim`/`bulletThickness`/`bulletTrail`/`bulletFlame`/`aoe*`/`orbit*`/`hitscan*`), because the combat core dispatches on presence.
- The Wave Laser's `hitscan` descriptor is carried as the flat pair `hitscanLength` / `hitscanDuration` (both blank for every non-hitscan weapon) so the beam length and visible duration stay designer-tunable and the wave laser round-trips through the CSV without a special case.
- `validateWeaponRow(row)` — rejects bad enums (`bulletShape`, `aoeTrigger`), non-hex colours, non-finite/negative numbers, unknown weapon ids, duplicate ids; returns a diagnostic naming the row and column.
- `parseWeaponCatalogue(weaponsCsv, patternsCsv): { catalogue, errors }` — merges both files; a row that fails validation falls back to the code default for that id with the diagnostic recorded (never throws).
- `serializeWeaponCatalogue(catalogue)` → `{ weaponsCsv, patternsCsv }` with the documented header comment block (column docs, `0xRRGGBB` note, degrees note), matching the `enemy-configs.csv` comment style.
- `fireRateMs` is **derived** from `subdivisions` through `beatSubdivisionMs` (`src/utils/beat.ts`), never stored — so the on-beat-grid invariant holds by construction.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The tests in child 1 pass.
2. Round-trip: `serializeWeaponCatalogue(parseWeaponCatalogue(x).catalogue)` re-parses to a deeply equal catalogue.
3. Every validation failure produces an actionable diagnostic (id + column + reason); malformed input never throws at the boundary.
4. Absent vs `0` semantics preserved for presence-dispatched fields (asserted).
5. `npm run typecheck` and the changed-scope tests pass; no behaviour change to `enemy-configs.csv` / `ship-config.csv` parsing (their tests stay green).

- `src/core/csv.ts` (extend)
- `src/utils/beat.ts` (read-only: `beatSubdivisionMs`)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` (types: `WeaponDefinition`, `BulletShape`, `OrbitDescriptor`, `AoEDescriptor`)

Child 1 (tests).

# Load the weapon catalogue from CSV (runtime source of truth + code fallback)

Parent: AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7.

## Goal

Make the parsed CSV the runtime source of truth for `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, with the TypeScript catalogue demoted to a fallback — following the established ladder used for `enemy-configs.csv` and `ship-config.csv`.

## Deliverables

- `src/core/bundledConfig.ts` — add `?raw` imports for `../data/weapons.csv` and `../data/weapon-patterns.csv`, exported alongside the existing bundled CSVs so the Vite build inlines them (production stays read-only, no runtime fetch).
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — rename the current literal to `DEFAULT_WEAPON_CATALOGUE` (internal fallback, still the authoritative shape/type reference) and expose `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` **built at module load** from `parseWeaponCatalogue(bundledWeaponsCsv, bundledWeaponPatternsCsv).catalogue`, falling back per-weapon to `DEFAULT_WEAPON_CATALOGUE` when a row is missing/invalid.
- `WEAPON_IDS: readonly WeaponId[]` — an explicit runtime id list (replacing reliance on `Record` key exhaustiveness), derived from the fallback catalogue so adding a weapon to the fallback keeps TS exhaustive.
- Boot-time self-check: a dev-only `console.warn` (or a diagnostic surfaced in the gym) listing any id that resolved from fallback instead of CSV, so a typo is visible rather than silent.
- Cadence ownership note in the module header (and on the `subdivisions`/`fireRateMs` fields): the catalogue value is the **legacy nominal** interval used for level-stat quantisation and the hold-full ghost metronome; the **live** cadence is `src/data/weapon-levels.json` (`resolveWeaponPattern`). A dev-only diagnostic warns when `subdivisions` disagrees with the ladder's level-0 rung density, naming `weapon-levels.json` as the cadence source.
- `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS` is **derived from the parsed catalogue** (`subdivisions` column) instead of a second hand-maintained literal, and `DEFAULT_RULES.weaponSubdivisions` seeds from it (`src/core/rules.ts`), so a designer's CSV fire-rate edit is not silently overridden by a stale code default. A persisted user override in the rules store still wins at runtime and is documented as a local, uncommitted setting.
- `getWeaponById` / `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` / `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS` keep their signatures — the 16 non-test consumers (`Player.ts`, `weaponLevels.ts`, `dropLayer.ts`, `dropDescriptions.ts`, `gymHelp.ts`, `captureCycle.ts`, `GymRhythm.ts`) are unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The parsed CSV is the single source of truth for runtime catalogue reads: editing `src/data/weapons.csv` or `src/data/weapon-patterns.csv` (e.g. `cannon` `bulletColor`) and refreshing `npm run dev` changes the live game with **no** TypeScript edit — demonstrated in the work-item comment.
2. `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` is populated from the CSV: a test asserts the runtime value differs from `DEFAULT_WEAPON_CATALOGUE` when the CSV is edited (mocked bundled import), and equals it for the committed seed.
3. A missing/invalid row falls back to the code default for that id only, leaving the remaining weapons CSV-driven.
4. `WEAPON_IDS` covers all 16 ids and `getWeaponById` throws/falls back identically for unknown ids as before.
5. No consumer file needs a change (assert by `git diff --stat`); typecheck clean, no behaviour change to any weapon (`resolveWeaponDefinition` output identical for level 0).
6. `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS` and `DEFAULT_RULES.weaponSubdivisions` are asserted equal to the catalogue's `subdivisions` for all 16 weapons, and a test proves editing the bundled CSV changes the derived default table (no second literal to drift).
7. The divergence diagnostic is tested both ways: silent when `subdivisions` matches the ladder's level-0 density (10 weapons), and a named warning for each of the six superposition weapons where the ladder is deliberate (cannon, rapid, arc, railgun, shard_swarm, heavy_slug) — asserted without changing gameplay.
6. Existing roster/doc-guard tests (`weaponVisualRoster.docs.test.ts`, `weaponFeelRoster.test.ts`, `powerUpWeaponRosterDocs.test.ts`) still pass unchanged, or are updated only to read the resolver rather than a literal.

## Key files

- `src/utils/weapons.ts`
- `src/core/bundledConfig.ts`
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` (verification only)

Children 2 and 3.

## Implementation clarification — AC7 divergence set (2026-11-04)

The AC7 wording ("silent for 10 weapons, a named warning for the six superposition weapons") was written against the **pre-trim** nominal subdivision table. The later level-0 output trim (AH-0MVWAVKS0005P9VN) lowered the nominal `subdivisions` of 13 non-cannon weapons without re-timing the Euclidean ladder, so the committed data now has **14 divergent / 2 identical** weapons (only `nova` and `mortar` agree).

Implemented as stated in spirit and proved both ways: the dev-only diagnostic is silent for the two matching weapons and names every divergent weapon — the six canonical superposition weapons (`cannon`, `rapid`, `arc`, `railgun`, `shard_swarm`, `heavy_slug`) remain in that warned set. The mismatch is surfaced (not hidden) and filed as **AH-0MW23FEDK006BRHK** ("Level-0 weapon output trim did not re-time the live Euclidean ladder"), which owns the producer decision on whether the trim should have changed live cadence. AC7's verification is the `src/utils/weaponDataDiagnostics.test.ts` suite.

## Implementation clarification — module cycle (2026-11-04)

Making `src/utils/weapons.ts` parse the CSV at module load exposed a latent module cycle: `csv.ts → configDefaults → constants → rules → weapons → csv.ts`. `constants.ts` had stopped being the leaf its header claims by importing `DEFAULT_RULES` for `POWER_UP_SPAWN_INTERVAL`; the parse then re-entered the half-initialised codec (`Cannot access 'WEAPON_ID_SET' before initialization`). Fixed by moving the `POWER_UP_SPAWN_INTERVAL` literal into the leaf `constants.ts` and having `rules.ts` seed `DEFAULT_POWER_UP_SPAWN_INTERVAL` from it (values unchanged: 12.5 s). `rules.ts` and `constants.ts` are the only files outside the listed consumer set touched; no listed consumer changed.

# Runtime invariant guards for the data-driven weapon catalogue

Parent: AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7.

## Goal

Replace the invariants that were previously guaranteed by the type system and by docs-guard tests with **runtime/data validation**, so a hand edit to the CSV cannot produce a silently broken roster.

## Deliverables

- `validateWeaponCatalogue(catalogue)` (in `src/core/csv.ts` or a `src/utils/weaponCatalogue.ts` leaf module) enforcing, per weapon and across the roster:
  - **on-beat grid:** every `fireRateMs` satisfies `isOnBeatGrid` (`src/utils/weapons.ts`), i.e. is an exact beat subdivision/multiple at the configured BPM;
  - **unique bullet-shape family:** no two weapons resolve the same canonical shape (`canonicalShape` collapsing the `circle`/`disc` alias), preserving the "every weapon is visually unique" roster guarantee;
  - **unique bullet colour** per weapon;
  - **sane magnitudes:** `bulletSize > 0`, `bulletLifetime > 0`, `aoeRadius >= 0`, `orbitRadius > 0` when `orbitPods` present, `bulletRim`/`impactColor`/`muzzleColor` in `0x000000–0xffffff`;
  - **structural coherence:** `aoeTrigger` present ⇒ `aoeRadius` present; `orbitPods` present ⇒ `orbitRadius` present; `splits`/`bounce`/`maxHitPoints` absent rather than `0` unless intentionally degenerate (flag with a warning).
- Wiring: the guard runs at catalogue build time (dev: surfaces diagnostics; prod: falls back to the code default for offending weapons) and is asserted directly by the test suite.
- Tests: one failing case per invariant (duplicate colour, duplicate shape family, off-beat rate, negative size, missing companion field), each asserting the diagnostic names the weapon id and the field.
- Update the existing docs-guard tests to assert against the parsed catalogue rather than the literal, so the same guarantee is checked for data edits.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Each invariant has at least one negative test proving the guard rejects it, and one positive test proving the committed seed passes.
2. An off-beat `fireRateMs` (e.g. from a hand-edited `subdivisions` of `1.37`) is rejected with a message that states the nearest on-grid value.
3. A duplicate colour/shape edit is rejected with both offending ids named.
4. Diagnostics are surfaced in dev (console/gym status) and never crash boot.
5. `weaponVisualRoster.docs.test.ts` and `weaponFeelRoster.test.ts` pass against the data-driven catalogue.
6. Malformed rows, unknown columns, invalid enums, off-beat fire rates, duplicate colours/shapes and out-of-range numbers are rejected with a diagnostic or fall back to the code default, and the game still boots.

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` (`isOnBeatGrid`, `canonicalShape`, `BULLET_COLORS`)
- `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts` (canonical shape helper)
- `src/utils/weaponVisualRoster.docs.test.ts`, `src/utils/weaponFeelRoster.test.ts` (update)

Child 4 (catalogue resolved from data).

# Docs: weapons CSV schema, retuning guide, invariants

Parent: AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7.

## Goal

Document the new designer workflow so retuning weapons needs no engineer and no archaeology, and so the invariants that used to be compiler-enforced are written down.

## Deliverables

- `docs/BALANCING.md` — new section "Weapon tuning CSV (AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7)":
  - where the files are (`src/data/weapons.csv`, `src/data/weapon-patterns.csv`) and what each column means (table mirroring the header comment);
  - the designer workflow (hand-edit → refresh; or panel → Save), and that a **rebuild is required for production** while dev reflects changes on refresh;
  - the "blank means absent" convention and why (`bounce`/`splits`/`maxHitPoints`/`aoe*`/`orbit*` presence drives dispatch);
  - angles authored in degrees, radians internally;
  - fire rate is authored as **shots per beat** and must stay on the beat grid (link to the beat-grid section already in that doc);
  - the invariants (unique shape family, unique colour, on-beat rates) and that they are runtime-validated with fallback to code defaults;
  - what a CSV row **cannot** do: add a weapon (needs an icon in `icons.ts` and a cue in `effects.ts`) or change the level ladder.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — extend the existing "Weapon Euclidean upgrade ladder" section: the ladders now live in `src/data/weapon-levels.json`; document the file shape (`weaponId` → ordered rungs of `{ k, n, rotation }`), the 16th-note lattice and derived step, how `minLevel` thresholds are derived from the `fireRate` curve, the fallback/precedence ladder, and that **this file, not `weapons.csv` `subdivisions`, is the live cadence**.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — note that the weapon panel is a tuning surface, not a gameplay gym, and that data-driven values must not diverge between `PlayScene` and the gyms.
- Code comments: `src/utils/weapons.ts` header explains the fallback ladder (`CSV → DEFAULT_WEAPON_CATALOGUE → per-weapon fallback`); `src/core/csv.ts` weapon codec section documents `WEAPON_COLUMN_ORDER` and the degrees/absent conventions.
- `README.md` — one-line pointer under the configuration section if it lists the CSV files today.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A designer who has never seen the repo can follow the doc to change a bullet colour, a fire rate and a Nova AoE radius, including how to verify the change.
2. Every column of `weapons.csv` appears in the table with units and legal values.

# Intake Brief: Move the weapon Euclidean level ladders to a data file

## Problem statement

`WEAPON_EUCLIDEAN_LADDER_SPECS` in `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` holds the per-weapon, per-level Euclidean cadence rungs `(k, n, rotation)` as hardcoded TypeScript. Designers cannot retune how a weapon's rhythm evolves across levels without editing TypeScript. This migration moves the authored pattern specs into `src/data/weapon-levels.json`, following the repo's precedent for nested data (e.g. `bot-tuning.json`).

**Adopted into AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7 (decision: option (b), 2026-11-03).** The catalogue's `subdivisions`/`fireRateMs` are **not** the live cadence: firing is driven by `resolveWeaponPattern` from this ladder (`Player._resolveFirePattern`, `src/entities/Player.ts:1416`), and `fireRateMs` only backs level-stat quantisation and the hold-full ghost metronome's nominal interval (`Player.getFireInterval`, consumed by `src/scenes/core/holdFullFire.ts`). The ladder is therefore the **single source of truth for fire cadence**, and `weapons.csv` `subdivisions` is documented as the legacy nominal value. This item is now a child of the epic and a prerequisite for its tuning panel, integration and docs children.

## Users

- **As a** game designer, **I want** to edit `weapon-levels.json` to change a weapon's Euclidean rhythm evolution across levels, **so that** I can tune combat feel without touching TypeScript or rebuilding.
- **As a** developer, **I want** the ladders to load from JSON with a code-default fallback on malformed data, **so that** the game never crashes at boot.
- **As a** reviewer, **I want** a frozen parity test proving `resolveWeaponPattern(weaponId, level)` output is unchanged for all 16 weapons at levels 0–10, **so that** the migration is provably zero-impact.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Data-driven:** `src/data/weapon-levels.json` stores the ladder specs keyed by `weaponId`, with each rung as `{ k, n, rotation }` (stepMs is a constant derived at runtime). Editing a rung in JSON changes `resolveWeaponPattern` output with no TypeScript edit — demonstrated in the work-item comment by changing one weapon's level-0 rung and observing the new onsets through `resolveWeaponPattern`/`getFirePattern`.
2. **Zero-impact migration:** A parity test proves `resolveWeaponPattern(weaponId, level)` returns the identical `EuclideanPattern` for all 16 shipped weapons at every level from 0 to 10, compared against the old in-code ladders.
3. **Monotonicity still holds:** The monotonic onsets-per-minute invariant and on-beat-grid guards from AH-0MVYA291J000CK64 still pass against the data-driven ladders.
4. **Graceful fallback:** Malformed or missing JSON falls back to the code ladder with a diagnostic console warning; boot never throws.
5. **Single source of truth for cadence:** the data-driven ladder is the only place a weapon's rhythm is authored. `weapons.csv` `subdivisions` remains the legacy **nominal** value; a dev-only diagnostic warns when it disagrees with the ladder's level-0 rung density (the six superposition weapons: cannon, rapid, arc, railgun, shard_swarm, heavy_slug), naming `weapon-levels.json` as the cadence source, so the divergence is visible rather than folklore.
6. **Documentation:** the JSON format, the `(k, n, rotation)` semantics, the 16th-note lattice, the derived upgrade thresholds and the load-order/fallback precedence are documented in `docs/BALANCING.md` alongside the weapon CSV section (content owned by this item, section owned by AH-0MW0Q1JK8001ZJ8I).

## Constraints

- **Nested structure → JSON, not CSV.** The per-weapon, per-level `(k, n, rotation)` rungs form a nested structure; `bot-tuning.json` is the established precedent.
- **Loader parity pattern.** Follow the existing weapon catalogue CSV→JSON→code-default fallback pattern (from AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7), reusing the shared loader infrastructure (`src/core/bundledConfig.ts`, `src/core/csv.ts` patterns).
- **Frozen parity fixture.** The parity test must compare against a golden snapshot, not against the old code default (to avoid the test regressing if the code default itself changes).
- **stepMs is constant.** All rungs share `SIXTEENTH_NOTE_STEP_MS`; the JSON stores only `{ k, n, rotation }` per rung, and `stepMs` is injected at load time.

## Existing state

- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — `WEAPON_EUCLIDEAN_LADDER_SPECS` (16 weapons, 2–6 rungs each) + `buildWeaponPatternLadder` (computes `minLevel` thresholds from `fireRate` curve) + `WEAPON_EUCLIDEAN_LADDERS` (final computed ladders) + `resolveWeaponPattern`.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.test.ts` — existing tests including monotonicity guards.
- `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — precedent for nested JSON data files with dev-panel write-back.
- `src/core/bundledConfig.ts` — `?raw` bundled import helper.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/weapon-levels.json` — new data file with ladder specs keyed by `weaponId`.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — modify to load from JSON; retain code ladder as fallback.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.test.ts` — add parity test; verify monotonicity tests still pass.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — document the JSON ladder format and load-order semantics.

## Out of scope (follow up if requested)

- A dev-panel **write path** for `weapon-levels.json` (GET/PUT via the `vite/plugins/botTuningPlugin.ts` precedent) and a Save control for rhythm. This item ships hand-edit only; the panel shows the ladder read-only and previews it.

## Related work

- **AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7** — parent epic. This item was formerly a `discovered-from` sibling and is now a child (option (b)).
- **AH-0MVYA291J000CK64** — Weapon upgrade ladder: monotonic density. The monotonicity and on-beat-grid guards from this completed item must still pass.

## Duplicate check

Performed — no overlapping completed items found.

## Problem

The level-0 output trim (AH-0MVWAVKS0005P9VN, parent AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T) was realised by **lowering the nominal fire-rate subdivisions** in `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` (`subdivisions` / `fireRateMs`) — spread 1→0.5, dual 1→0.5, rapid 6→3, ricochet 1→0.5, cluster 0.5→0.25, options 1→0.5, rear_guard 2→1, broadside 0.5→0.25, shard_swarm 1→0.5, heavy_slug 0.5→0.25. It did **not** change `WEAPON_EUCLIDEAN_LADDER_SPECS`, and player firing is driven by the Euclidean ladder (`Player._resolveFirePattern` → `resolveWeaponPattern`), not by `fireRateMs`.

Consequence: the live level-0 cadence was not actually slowed by the trim, so the "≤ 60 % of the pre-change level-0 output" claim may not hold for the shipped game; the balance measurements in `src/utils/weapons.test.ts` (`LEVEL0_TRIMMED`) are computed from the nominal subdivision and therefore measure a cadence the game does not play.

## Evidence

Discovered while implementing AH-0MW0Q1EYJ007RRFI (which makes the CSV the runtime catalogue source and adds the cadence-divergence diagnostic). The diagnostic reports **14 of 16 weapons** whose nominal `subdivisions` disagrees with the live level-0 ladder density (only nova and mortar agree):

- cannon 2 vs 2.25, rapid 3 vs 3.25, arc 1 vs 2.25, railgun 0.25 vs 0.5, shard_swarm 0.5 vs 2.5, heavy_slug 0.25 vs 0.75 (the six canonical superposition weapons, deliberately irregular);
- spread/dual/wave_laser/ricochet/options/rear_guard 0.5-1 vs 1-2, cluster/broadside 0.25 vs 0.5 (straight ladders whose nominal was lowered by the trim without re-timing the ladder).

The work item's original "10 silent / six named" expectation was written against the pre-trim subdivision table; it no longer describes the committed data.

## Expected outcome

Decide (producer call) whether the trim was intended to change the *live* cadence:

1. **If yes:** re-time the level-0 ladder rungs (or apply a trim multiplier to `_resolveFirePattern`) so live output matches the measured ≤ 60 % target, then re-baseline `LEVEL0_TRIMMED` and the balance docs.
2. **If no:** correct the trim's documentation/measurements to use the live ladder density, and update `AH-0MW0Q1TQV009M8AO` AC5 (the same six-weapon expectation) to match the real divergence set.

Either way, the cadence-divergence diagnostic added by AH-0MW0Q1EYJ007RRFI now surfaces the mismatch at dev boot.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The intended live level-0 output is confirmed (trim live or nominal-only), recorded on this item, and reconciled with the strength-budget documentation.
2. The balance measurement in `weapons.test.ts` measures the live cadence (the Euclidean ladder) rather than the nominal subdivision.
3. The cadence-divergence set after the fix is either empty or matches the documented, deliberate superposition set, and the dev diagnostic agrees.
4. Full suite green (`/skill:test`), typecheck clean.

Discovered from: AH-0MW0Q1EYJ007RRFI (runtime catalogue CSV load + cadence diagnostic).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVYA1V8Z009SHMR** – Fire scheduler: Euclidean pattern as the fire cadence with synced VFX/SFX (completed)
- **AH-0MW0Q1EYJ007RRFI** – Load the weapon catalogue from CSV (runtime source of truth + code fallback) (completed)

- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: 0mvreneme004fs8t, 0mw0q1tqv009m8ao, ac5, acceptance, adds (+129 more)


## Decision (producer, recorded during plan)

**Option 1 — re-time the live Euclidean ladder.** The level-0 trim is intended to reach the player.

Planning findings (full analysis in the plan comments):

- The intended trim maps onto the ladder as an integer `k` with `n = 16` and the 187.5 ms 16th-note step retained. The largest compliant `k` for every breaching weapon is exactly `4 x subdivisions`: spread 4->2, dual 4->2, ricochet 4->2, options 4->2, rear_guard 8->4, cluster 2->1, broadside 2->1, arc 9->4, shard_swarm 10->2, heavy_slug 3->1.
- Five weapons are already compliant and need no ladder change (rapid 54 %, wave_laser 50 %, nova 57 %, mortar 60 %, railgun 40 %); cannon is frozen/exempt.
- The `<= 60 %` budget forces arc/shard_swarm/heavy_slug into straight patterns, so the pinned 46-onsets/bar canonical superposition fixture is re-baselined to 31 onsets/bar.
- Re-timing level 0 alone breaches `level1GrowthMultiple` (2.5x) for cluster/broadside/shard_swarm/heavy_slug, so the trim must either cascade up the ladder or the ceiling must be re-baselined — **open producer question (see comments)**.
- After the fix the remaining cadence divergence is cannon (9 vs 8), rapid (13 vs 12) and railgun (2 vs 1) — all deliberate superposition members — plus wave_laser, whose nominal `subdivisions` is corrected 0.5 -> 1 (documentation-only, no cadence change).

## Producer decision — Option 1a (cascade), confirmed

The producer answered the open question from the plan comments: **Option 1a — cascade the trim up the whole ladder.** Recorded here so implementation cannot drift from it.

- **Level 0** of each affected weapon is re-timed so its live Euclidean density equals the already-trimmed nominal `subdivisions` in `src/data/weapons.csv` (spread 0.5, dual 0.5, ricochet 0.5, options 0.5, rear_guard 1, cluster 0.25, broadside 0.25, arc 1, shard_swarm 0.5, heavy_slug 0.25 onsets/beat).

- **wave_laser**: nominal `subdivisions` corrected 0.5 -> 1 (data/documentation only, no cadence change) because its live density is already compliant.
- **Unchanged ladders**: rapid, nova, mortar, railgun (already inside the level-0 bound) and cannon (frozen/exempt).
- The canonical six-weapon superposition fixture re-baselines from 46 to 31 onsets/bar; arc, shard_swarm and heavy_slug become straight (degenerate) patterns under the <= 60 % budget, a documented design artefact.
- **Measurement fix (AC2)**: `weaponStrength` currently derives `shotsPerSecond` from the nominal `fireRateMs` (which comes from `subdivisions`), so it measures a cadence the game does not play. It must derive cadence from the live ladder (`resolveWeaponPattern` -> onsets/minute), which is what `Player._resolveFirePattern` actually schedules.
- **Diagnostic (AC3)**: after the fix the remaining nominal-vs-live divergences are exactly cannon (2 vs 2.25), rapid (3 vs 3.25) and railgun (0.25 vs 0.5) — the deliberate superposition set — so the dev boot diagnostic must treat the documented deliberate set as informational (no warning) and stay loud for anything else.

## Problem

`scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune` edits a tracked balance CSV in place and journals the pre-edit bytes beside it (`src/data/<file>.tune-journal`). Both paths are process-global, not per-run:

1. **Startup reconcile steals a live journal.** `main()` reconciles `<csv>.tune-journal` before anything else (crash recovery). A journal is written before the edit and removed after the restore, so it exists for the whole candidate sweep of a *running* process — a second `--tune` run on the same CSV reconciles it, restoring the CSV underneath run 1.
2. **Two runs interleave edits.** Run 2 writes its own journal over run 1's, then restores from run 2's bytes while run 1 continues its candidate sweep against a file run 2 may have rewritten.

Discovered while fixing AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS: the `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` watchdog case asserted "no `*.tune-journal` anywhere in `src/data`", which failed when a sibling suite in the same parallel Vitest run held a journal at the same shared path. The suite was fixed for the shared path (the assertion is now scoped to the run's own pid), but the product-level hazard remains for real concurrent CLI invocations.

## Impact

Two designers (or a designer plus a scripted tuning sweep) tuning the same balance CSV at once can silently produce a comparison against the wrong CSV bytes, and the crash-recovery journal can be consumed by the wrong run. Single-run usage is unaffected.

## Suggested approach

Pick one, cheapest first:

- **Lock file**: an exclusive `<csv>.tune-lock` (O\_EXCL) held for the whole run, with a bounded wait and a clear exit-2 diagnostic naming the holder pid. The journal's pid is already recorded, so the holder is identifiable.
- **Refuse concurrent runs**: on `writeJournal`, if a journal exists whose pid is alive (`kill(pid, 0)`), abort with exit 2 naming that pid instead of overwriting it.
- **Per-run temp CSVs**: out of scope — `--tune` deliberately edits the tracked file so the candidate sweep reads it through the shared config store.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Two concurrent `--tune` runs on the same CSV cannot interleave: the second either waits (bounded) or exits non-zero with a diagnostic naming the holding pid.
2. A live journal is never reconciled by another process: crash recovery only consumes a journal whose pid is dead.
3. `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` and `scripts/csvEditJournal.test.ts` still pass, including the pid-scoped journal assertions added by AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS.
4. `docs/BALANCING.md` documents the concurrency rule alongside the crash-safe journal section.
5. Full suite passes (`/skill:test`).

## Related work

- discovered-from:AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS (the test-failure item that surfaced the shared-path race).

## Goal

Restore **hardware-GPU access for the frame-time harness on the reference host**, so AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P (hardware-GPU desktop verification) can record the two runs its acceptance criteria require. This is an **operator/machine task**: every step needs `sudo`, a re-login or physical access, so it cannot be completed by an agent session.

**User story:** As the producer, I want the reference host to expose a working hardware GPU driver to the measuring user, so the 60 FPS desktop target can be measured on a real GPU instead of a software rasteriser.

## Measured state (2026-11-04, commit `da8aaa8f`, host `rgardler` reference machine)

The host **does** have GPU hardware: `lspci` shows `NVIDIA GA107M [GeForce RTX 3050 Ti Mobile]` (01:00.0) and `AMD Renoir [Radeon Vega Series]` (06:00.0); `nvidia_uvm`/`nvidia_drm`/`amdgpu` are loaded. Two independent, separately fixable faults stop the harness from using either one as a WebGL backend.

### 1. NVIDIA: kernel module and userspace driver disagree (MOOT until reboot)

- `nvidia-smi` → `Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch` (`NVML library version: 595.99`).
- `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` → `NVRM version: ... 595.91.07` (kernel module), while the installed userspace is `nvidia-driver-595-open 595.99.02-0ubuntu0.26.04.1`; the host has been up 2 days 23 h, so the module predates the last driver upgrade.
- The device nodes themselves are **not** the problem: `/dev/nvidia0`, `/dev/nvidiactl`, `/dev/nvidia-uvm` and `/dev/nvidia-modeset` are mode `666` and open successfully as the non-root measuring user.
- A mismatched kernel/userspace pair cannot create a GL or Vulkan context, so `--gpu` cannot reach the RTX 3050 Ti in this state even though the nodes are writable.
- **Fix:** reboot (loads the matching 595.99 module set), or reload the module without a reboot (`sudo systemctl stop gdm` then `sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia_modeset nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia`), then confirm `nvidia-smi` reports the GPU.

### 2. AMD iGPU: DRM render nodes are not accessible to the measuring user

- `/dev/dri/renderD128` (Renoir, 06:00.0), `/dev/dri/renderD129` (NVIDIA), `card0`, `card1` are `root:video` / `root:render`, mode `660`, with an ACL granting only `gdm-greeter`.
- `uid=1000(rgardler)` groups: `adm, cdrom, sudo, dip, plugdev, users, lpadmin, lxd` — **not** `video` or `render`. Opening any of the four nodes fails with `EACCES` (`Permission denied`), so Mesa/radv/ANGLE cannot enumerate a hardware device.
- **Fix (either):** `sudo usermod -aG video,render rgardler` then fully re-login (group membership is per-session); **or** run the measurement from the graphical seat session, where logind grants the seat user the device ACL.

### 3. No display server, and Electron is no longer installed

- `DISPLAY` is unset and there is no Xorg/Xvfb, so a *windowed* hardware run needs a seat. This does not block the measurements themselves: `--ozone-platform=headless` (Electron) and headless Chromium both work, and the harness's window-visibility guard covers the Electron case.
- `node_modules/electron` is **absent** in the main checkout, so `--host electron` stops with "Electron is not installed" — even the software Electron row is currently not reproducible here. `electron` is an `optionalDependencies` entry, so a plain `npm install` prunes it again; install it explicitly (`npm install electron@^45.2.2`) before the Electron runs.

### Harness guard re-verified (both desktop hosts, short guard-check runs)

| Invocation | Result |
|---|---|
| `--gpu --require-hardware-webgl --scene GymPerformance --seconds 3 --warmup 1` | exit 1: *"Refusing to publish a hardware-GPU baseline: the page rendered on a software WebGL backend (ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device (Subzero) (0x0000C0DE)), SwiftShader driver))"* |
| `--host electron --gpu --require-hardware-webgl ...` | exit 1: *"Electron is not installed, so `--host electron` cannot run."* |

So the guard behaves correctly: it refuses to publish a software run as a desktop hardware baseline. The gap is host access, not harness behaviour.

## Scope

- Bring up a working hardware GPU backend for the measuring user on the reference host (`nvidia-smi` reports the GPU; a Vulkan/GL context is creatable as `rgardler`; `/dev/dri/render*` openable or an equivalent working path).
- Install the (optional) `electron` dependency so `--host electron` can launch.
- Report back which driver path is available (NVIDIA proprietary vs AMD Mesa) and the renderer string a browser reports, so the verification run can be scheduled.

## Out of scope

- The verification runs themselves and the `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` records — they stay in AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P.
- Any optimisation work, harness change or target change.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `nvidia-smi` (or an equivalent AMD/Mesa query) reports a GPU usable by the non-root measuring user, and the raw cause of the current fault (NVML driver/library mismatch / device-node `EACCES`) no longer applies.
2. `node_modules/electron` is installed and `npx electron --version` succeeds.
3. A headless Chromium launched with `--gpu` reports a **non-SwiftShader** `WEBGL_debug_renderer_info` string (the string recorded in the completion comment) — i.e. `--require-hardware-webgl` passes.
4. The exact steps taken (commands, group/ACL changes, driver/reboot path) are recorded in a completion comment so the reference machine stays reproducible.

## Goal

Make the frame-time harness's `--gpu` path actually reach a hardware WebGL backend, so `--require-hardware-webgl` can pass on the reference host now that AH-0MW2L3JXU008I2Z8 has restored the NVIDIA driver.

**User story:** As the producer, I want `measure-performance.mjs --gpu --require-hardware-webgl` to render on the real GPU on a hardware host, so the desktop 60 FPS target can be measured instead of being blocked by a SwiftShader refusal.

## Problem (measured, 2026-11-04, reference host, driver 595.99.02)

`rendererSwitches(gpu)` in `scripts/perf-launch.mjs` contributes only `--ignore-gpu-blocklist` and `--enable-gpu-rasterization` for a `--gpu` run. On this host Chromium still selects SwiftShader for those args alone; only an explicit ANGLE-Vulkan request reaches the GPU:

| Args | `WEBGL_debug_renderer_info` |
|---|---|
| harness `--gpu` as-is | `ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device (Subzero) (0x0000C0DE)), SwiftShader driver)` |
| `+ --use-gl=angle --use-angle=vulkan` | `ANGLE (NVIDIA, Vulkan 1.4.329 (NVIDIA NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU (0x000025A0)), NVIDIA)` |
| `+ --use-angle=gl` / `+ --use-gl=egl` / `+ --enable-features=Vulkan` | SwiftShader |

Consequence: `node scripts/measure-performance.mjs --scene GymPerformance --seconds 3 --warmup 1 --gpu --require-hardware-webgl` exits 1 with the software-backend refusal on a host whose GPU is fully working.

## Desired change

Extend the `--gpu` switch set (`HARDWARE_SWITCHES` / `rendererSwitches()`) with the ANGLE-Vulkan pair so Chromium asks for the hardware backend, keeping the same switch set for the browser and Electron hosts (they share `rendererSwitches()`). Preserve the software path for runs without `--gpu` (SwiftShader must still be selectable so software baselines stay reproducible).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `rendererSwitches({ gpu: true })` includes the ANGLE-Vulkan selection, and `rendererSwitches({ gpu: false })` is unchanged — asserted in `scripts/perf-launch.test.ts`.
2. `node scripts/measure-performance.mjs --scene GymPerformance --seconds 3 --warmup 1 --gpu --require-hardware-webgl` exits 0 on the reference host and its JSON report carries a non-SwiftShader renderer string (the string recorded in the completion comment).
3. The change also applies to `--host electron` (shared `rendererSwitches()`), verified once `electron` is installed — or a comment records why it cannot be verified yet.
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (in particular `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`'s hardware-GPU baseline section).
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Related

- Discovered from **AH-0MW2L3JXU008I2Z8** (host GPU access restored; AC3 needs this harness change).
- Blocks **AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P** (hardware-GPU desktop verification runs).

- `scripts/perf-launch.test.ts` — unit tests for `rendererSwitches()` / launch arg builders.

## Problem / goal

The repo can measure one fixed load (`GymPerformance`, exactly 100 enemies with
live fire — AH-0MVXV0DT50028RF8) but there is no repeatable way to answer "how
many enemies can we actually hold at a playable frame rate?". The producer has
to pick the load by hand, run the harness several times, and reconcile the
numbers themselves.

As the producer, I want **a performance testing skill** that automatically
walks the enemy load upward in 50-enemy steps until the game stops being
playable, so I get a headroom curve (min / max / average FPS per load) from one
command instead of a series of ad-hoc runs.

## Expected behaviour

Invoking the skill (e.g. `/skill:perf-sweep`, final name to be decided at plan
time) runs a **sweep**:

1. **Load steps of 50 enemies**, starting at 50 (`50, 100, 150, …`).
2. At every step the measured load is **enemies that both shoot and dive** —
   live fire and diving behaviour on screen, not idle targets.
3. At every step the **player has a full loadout of weaponry and upgrades,
   chosen at random** for that step (all weapon slots and the upgrade/power-up
   set maxed, per whatever "full loadout" resolves to in `GameState` /
   `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`). The chosen loadout is recorded with the step.
4. Each step is measured for **at least 15 seconds** (warm-up excluded from the
   measurement window, and reported).
5. Per step record **min, max and average FPS** (plus p50/p95 frame time, long
   frames, and live enemy/bullet counts — the harness already produces these).
6. **Iterate until a step's average FPS is below 30**, then stop: that step is
   the reported failure point and the previous step is the last playable load.
   A hard ceiling (e.g. 400 enemies) and a total-run budget guard against a
   runaway sweep.
7. **Report the results to the user** at the end: a summary table of every step
   (enemy count, loadout, min/average/max FPS, verdict) plus the headline
   ("playable to N enemies; first failure at M with average X FPS") and the path
   to the machine-readable JSON report.

## Design outline (to be confirmed at plan time)

- Reuse the existing harness rather than writing a second one:
  `scripts/measure-performance.mjs` (`perfProbe`, `--seconds`, `--warmup`,
  `--cpu-throttle`, `--scene`, `--out`) and its pure maths in
  `scripts/perf-report.mjs`.
- The scene must accept an **enemy count parameter** plus a **full-loadout
  setup** and include diving archetypes. Options to choose between at plan
  time: (a) parameterise `GymPerformance`/`GymFormationScene` (it already takes
  `config.count` and `buildOffsets(count)`) rather than adding a scene; or
  (b) add a sweep gym. Preference is (a) — one scene, one code path, no
  divergence — with the parity matrix updated only if a new scene is genuinely
  required.
- The loadout must be applied through the shipped/shared path (no test-only
  re-implementation of weapon or upgrade behaviour), so the measured frame cost
  is the frame cost a player would pay.
- The sweep orchestration should be a small, unit-testable pure planner (step
  list, stop rule, summary) driven by a thin CLI/script, so the stop rule and
  summary are tested without booting a browser.
- Random loadout selection must be **seeded and recorded**, so a run can be
  reproduced (`seed` in the report; same seed → same loadout sequence).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A performance-testing skill exists, is discoverable by name, and its
   documentation states the sweep, the load definition, the 15 s minimum
   measurement window and the stop rule.
2. One command runs the whole sweep unattended on the reference host: enemies
   in 50-enemy increments, each step with enemies that shoot **and** dive, and
   with a randomly chosen **full** weapon/upgrade loadout for the player.
3. Every step measures for **at least 15 seconds** (warm-up excluded) and
   records **min, max and average FPS**, alongside the frame-time percentiles,
   long-frame counts and live enemy/bullet counts.
4. The sweep stops at the **first step whose average FPS is below 30**, records
   that step as the failure point, and reports the previous step as the last
   playable load; a documented ceiling/timeout prevents a runaway sweep.
5. The final report is printed to the user as a per-step table plus a headline
   verdict, and the same data is written to a machine-readable JSON report that
   names the scene, step list, loadout per step, seed, host and commit.
6. The random loadout is seeded and recorded; re-running with the same seed
   produces the same loadout sequence (unit-tested).
7. The step planner, stop rule and summary are covered by fast unit tests (no
   browser); the scene's parameterised enemy count and loadout seam are covered
   by scene tests; the full suite is green via the test skill and typecheck is
   clean.
8. Gym↔game parity is preserved: the measured scenario runs shared core code,
   any new/changed gym is registered in the capture registry and
   `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, and no simulation loop is forked.
9. Usage is documented (skill docs plus a link from the performance docs /
   README harness section) and one recorded sweep on the reference host is
   published with the provenance the `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` "Recorded:" rule
   requires (commit, date, host, backend, throttle).

## Out of scope

- Optimising anything found by the sweep (a regression or hotspot becomes its
  own child/discovered-from item, per parent AC6).
- Changing the existing budget (60 FPS desktop / >= 30 FPS mobile) or the
  existing `GymPerformance` 100-enemy rows.
- Mobile/CPU-throttled sweeps (the skill may accept `--cpu-throttle` as a
  pass-through, but no throttled sweep is recorded by this item).
- Electron-host sweeps beyond what the existing harness already supports.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPerformance.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`
  — parameterise the enemy count and the player loadout (`config.count`,
  `buildOffsets(count)`, `createEnemyFromConfig`, `fireForEnemy`).
- `src/core/perfProbe.ts` — the probe and `PerformanceCounts` seam the sweep
  samples (no change expected).
- `scripts/measure-performance.mjs`, `scripts/perf-launch.mjs`,
  `scripts/perf-report.mjs` — the harness the sweep drives.
- `scripts/perf-sweep.mjs` *(new, likely)* — step planner + sweep driver.
- `src/core/GameState.ts`, `src/core/rules.ts` (`POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`,
  `defaultPowerUpWeights`), `src/utils/weapons.ts`,
  `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — where a full loadout is granted.
- `.pi/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` *(new)* — the skill itself (project-local;
  see Open Questions).
- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`, `README.md` — usage + the recorded sweep.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`,
  `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` — only if a gym changes/arrives.

## Open questions (to resolve at plan time)

1. **Where does the skill live?** Project-local `.pi/skills/<name>/` (travels
   with the repo and can reference the repo's harness) vs a global skill in
   `~/.pi/agent/skills/`. Recommendation: project-local, because the sweep is
   specific to this harness/scene; note that editing `.pi/` is normally
   restricted and this item is the explicit instruction to do so.
2. **"Full loadout" definition** — which weapons/upgrades, whether the loadout
   is a random subset of a maxed set or a random arrangement across fixed
   maxed slots, and whether power-up *levels* are maxed too. Needs a concrete,
   testable definition.
3. **"Shoot and dive" mix** — which archetypes are the shooting and diving
   members of each step and in what proportion (the existing stress gym roster
   already includes `diver` and `raider`; confirm the intended mix and pin it
   in a test).
4. **Does the player shoot?** The stress gym disables player auto-fire so the
   100-enemy load cannot decay. A full loadout implies the player *is* firing,
   which changes the load (bullets + kills) — decide whether enemies are kept
   alive (invulnerable/respawning) so the enemy count stays fixed for the whole
   window, and record that decision in the report.
5. **Reproduce the load** — with player fire enabled the load becomes
   time-dependent; decide how the sweep keeps steps comparable (fixed seed,
   fixed step duration, kill-free enemies, or a documented "as-played" mode).

## Notes / constraints

- Measurement policy: agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill; the
  sweep itself is a measurement tool, not a test run, and must not be wired
  into the vitest suite (same rule the existing harness follows).
- Noise floor: compare only within one host load band, and record the host,
  backend and load per step (parent AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87 AC6, and the
  `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` noise-floor rule).
- The host can be busy with other agents' suites; the sweep should record each
  step's host load so a noisy sweep is identifiable rather than silently
  published.

## Related work

- `discovered-from:AH-0MW3KP1R90030QY9` — filed while re-measuring the mobile
  tier on hardware WebGL; the sweep is the natural next step after the fixed
  100-enemy rows.
- Related: **Optimization pass** (AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87) and its performance
  children — **Frame-time performance harness for `PlayScene` (headless
  p50/p95/FPS)** (AH-0MVXV0DER009ER70), **`GymPerformance` stress gym — 100
  late-game enemies with live fire** (AH-0MVXV0DT50028RF8), **Publish
  performance budget, harness usage and results
  (docs/PERFORMANCE.md)** (AH-0MVXV0FUP006W8OR), **Re-measure the mobile tier
  on hardware WebGL and close parent AC5 (4x CPU throttle, quiet host)**
  (AH-0MW3KP1R90030QY9).
- Related: **Increase the possible number of enemies in a enemy formation to
  200** (AH-0MTV8Q1LV001KOA5) — the formation cap bounds how large a sweep step
  can be; confirm it before claiming a 200+ step is reachable.
data.title: Performance testing skill — 50-enemy FPS sweep with a full random loadout

# Halve the per-kill drop-chance defaults and add the rules v5 migration

## Goal

**User story:** As a player, I want at most half as many power-ups per kill as
today, and no extra lives from asteroids, so each pickup feels earned — tuned
from **one** shared place.

Implementation item for the parent's AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC5
(AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM). It turns the test-first item red→green.

## What to do

- `src/core/rules.ts`
  - `DEFAULT_POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE_AT_LEVEL_1` `0.18 → 0.09`.
  - `DEFAULT_POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE_AT_MAX_LEVEL` `0.05 → 0.025`.
  - `DEFAULT_ASTEROID_EXTRA_LIFE_DROP_CHANCE` `0.05 → 0`.
  - `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION` `4 → 5`, with a v5 branch in `loadRules` that
    **resets** `powerUpDropChanceAtLevel1`, `powerUpDropChanceAtMaxLevel` and
    `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` to the new defaults for any blob older than
    version 5 (same precedent as the v2/v3 resets), so a `saveRules`-written
    `0.18`/`0.05` cannot silently defeat the change.
  - Update the default-chance doc comments (values, rationale, item id).
- `src/core/levelScaling.ts` — doc comments and the `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE`
  re-export follow the new level-1 value; **no formula change** (the ramp and
  the max-level clamp stay as they are).
- `src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.ts` — comment only: the rule is retained
  and configurable, defaulted off.
- Do **not** change any drop weight (Extra Life stays `3`), the 5-life cap or
  the `lifeGain` curve.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `powerUpDropChance(level)` is exactly half its former value at every level
  1–10, and the L10/L1 ratio stays ≈ 0.278.
- `DEFAULT_EXTRA_LIFE_WEIGHT === 3` and no other weight changed (Extra
  Life stays ≈ 5.2 % of power-up draws; only the per-kill roll halves).
- A fully destroyed small asteroid never spawns `extra_life` at the default
  chance, in `PlayScene` and in every asteroid-bearing gym
  (`GymFormationScene`, `GymMinerals`, `GymLevel`) — proven through the shared
  `rollAsteroidExtraLife` rule, not a scene bypass.
- The asteroid rule, its `GameRules` key, its clamping and its persistence
  all remain, so a designer can re-enable it with one config value.
- Old blobs migrate to the new defaults; blobs stamped `version: 5` keep
  their tuned values.
- No scene, gym or test hard-codes the new numbers — all tuning flows from
  `src/core/rules.ts` / `src/core/levelScaling.ts`.
- The test-first item's tests pass, and the touched suites
  (`rules`, `levelScaling`, `asteroidKillDrops`, gym fixtures that force
  `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance: 1` and must now stamp
  `version: RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION`) are green.

- **Covers parent AC1:** Per-kill drop rate halved: `DEFAULT_POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE_AT_LEVEL_1` is `0.09` (was `0.18`) and `DEFAULT_POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE_AT_MAX_LEVEL` is `0.025` (was `0.05`), so `powerUpDropChance(level)` from `src/core/levelScaling.ts` is half its former value at every level of the 1–10 campaign while keeping the linear ramp (L10 stays ≈ 27.8 % of L1). The re-exported `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE` (documented level-1 base) becomes `0.09`. Verified by unit tests on the defaults and on the curve endpoints plus an intermediate level.
- **Covers parent AC2:** No double-halving of Extra Life's share: `DEFAULT_EXTRA_LIFE_WEIGHT` stays `3` and no other drop weight changes, so Extra Life's *relative* rarity in the shared pool (≈ 5.2 % of power-up draws) is untouched — only the per-kill roll falls. Its absolute per-kill chance at L1 drops from ≈ 0.93 % to ≈ 0.47 %. Verified by a rules/spawner-share test.
- **Covers parent AC3:** Asteroids stop dropping Extra Life: `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` defaults to `0` (was `0.05`); the shared rule (`rollAsteroidExtraLife`), the `GameRules` key and its clamping/persistence stay in place so a designer can re-enable it. ## Goal

**User story:** As a player, I want the hold-full and mini-boss rewards to
offer upgrades rather than a life top-up, so the reward moment is about
building the ship — while Extra Life stays a rare field pickup.

  existing `rewardableWhenOwned` precedent in `src/powerups/types.ts`: a
  catalogue flag or a single exported exclusion set consumed by every

  it gets no `power-up-level` Extra Life option.

# Intake brief — Text on hex map is unreadable (AH-0MW3VG6WJ004HRI9)

## Headline

The hex map's hex tiles render their full known-ahead intel block at 7px on a
960×540 canvas, so the information the design promises ("known-ahead intel",
`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D) is unreadable. Redesign the tile to
carry only the aggression level at a readable size and move the full intel into
a detail panel that follows the focused hex.

## Problem statement

Every hex tile on the map (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` `renderHexTile`)
currently prints the entire intel payload — hex id, held/unheld, aggression,
incoming force, boss, strengths, weaknesses, granted weapon and any defender or
attack resolution — as 7px monospace text inside a 50px tile. At 960×540 the
text is physically too small to read, which defeats the design's known-ahead
intel promise (a plan must be formable *before* a life is spent).

## Users

The player navigating the Hangar War map; the map is also rendered read-only in
the `GymHexWar` parity gym for testing and capture.

- As a player, I want to see at a glance how dangerous each hex is, so I can
  scan the ring quickly. *→ aggression on the tile.*
- As a player, I want to read the full details of the hex I am considering
  before I commit to a deployment. *→ detail panel for the focused hex.*
- As a player, I want the same interaction model as before (keyboard
  tab/arrows move focus, Enter/click deploys), so learning the map is not
  re-learned.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Short tile label:** each hex tile renders only its aggression (`AGG n`)
   as its on-tile text, at a readable font size (no full intel block on tiles,
   no sub-10px tile text). Held/unheld remains conveyed by tile colour.
2. **Detail panel:** the map shows a panel with the full known-ahead intel of
   the selected hex — hex id, held/unheld, aggression and incoming force, boss,
   strengths, weaknesses, granted weapon/upgrade, defender and any queued
   attack resolution — at a readable font size.
3. **Selection follows focus:** the panel updates to the **focused** hex
   (keyboard tab/arrows; pointer-over may also drive it). Enter/click still
   deploys at the focused hex. In read-only renders (the parity gym passes no
   handlers) the panel defaults to the model's default/first hex so the gym
   still shows detail.
4. **Gym↔game parity:** `GymHexWar` renders the same tiles and panel through
   the shared `renderHexMap`/model (no divergent copy); `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`
   stays accurate.
5. **Validation/tests:** `HexMapScene.test.ts`, `GymHexWar.test.ts` and
   `hexIntel.test.ts` updated to assert the short tile label and the panel's
   full-intel content for the focused hex; new test covers the read-only
   default-panel case.
6. **Docs:** all related documentation updated to reflect the changes,
   including code comments, README, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`/`docs/GYM_PARITY.md`
   where they describe the map surface.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep the gym↔game parity: behaviour change must land in the shared
  renderer/model, not a divergent copy in one scene.
- Preserve the known-ahead intel promise — the full detail must remain
  readable *before* deployment, which the panel satisfies.
- Do not change the deployment action model: focused hex + Enter/click deploys;
  no arcade-checkpoint involvement.
- 960×540 canvas; tile geometry (`HEX_SIZE = 50`, pointy-top axial layout) is
  not in scope to change unless required.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — shared renderer: tiles print
  `intel.label` (the full block) at `7px`; legend lists every symbol; a
  `FocusManager` already handles keyboard focus and `pointerover` styling.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — pure model: `hexLabel()` builds the full
  multi-line `label`; `HexIntel` carries all fields the panel needs.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — game scene wiring the renderer to deploy /
  open-hangar handlers; `getFocusedKey()`/`focusRow()` seams already exist.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — parity gym calling `renderHexMap(this,
  model)` with **no handlers** (read-only; currently nothing is focusable there
  because rows register only when actionable).
- Tests: `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts` (asserts `row.label` equals the full
  intel block), `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts` (same), `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts`
  (model label content).

## Desired change

- Tiles: replace the full-block `intel.label` text with a short aggression-only
  label (`AGG n`), rendered at a readable size; keep the coloured tile body.
- Add a detail panel (e.g. right-hand side of the map) rendering the selected
  hex's full intel — reusing the model's full `label` text or a structured
  rendering of the `HexIntel` fields — at a readable size, updated on focus
  change; default to the model's default/first hex when nothing is focused
  (read-only renders).
- Update the legend to describe the new surface (aggression tiles + detail
  panel) and update the tests/docs to match.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — short tile label, new detail panel, legend
  update (shared by game and gym).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — model: add/provide a short tile label
  alongside the full `label` if the panel needs structured fields.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — only if the panel needs scene-level wiring
  (e.g. focus-change hookup); likely minimal.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — verify read-only default-panel behaviour.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts` — updated assertions.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — parity/design docs if
  they describe tile content.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep risk:** keep the change to tile label + panel; any extra
  readability work (other scene font sizes, panel styling polish) is tracked as
  separate items, not added here.
- **Assumption:** "selected hex" == focused hex (operator-confirmed Q2, option
  A); pointer-over may additionally drive the panel.
- **Assumption:** tile shows *only* `AGG n` (operator-confirmed Q1, option A);
  hex id is not shown on the tile.
- **Parity risk:** the gym renders with no handlers, so nothing is focusable;
  the panel must fall back to the model default/first hex there or the gym loses
  the panel. Explicit AC 3 covers this.
- **Test drift:** existing tests assert `row.label` equals the full intel block;
  they must be re-pointed at the panel, not deleted.

## Related work

- AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2 "Hex map scene with known-ahead intel" (completed) — the
  scene this fix refines; its design doc references apply.
- AH-0MVUXC9KG008G80Y "Hex ring model, generator and ring 1/2 definitions"
  (completed) — ring/definitions the map renders.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (Candidate D) — known-ahead intel and
  anti-checklist mitigations; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — parity record.
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping open/completed item found for
  unreadable hex-map text.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What remains on each hex tile?" — Answer (operator, interactive reply):
  "(a) Only `AGG n` (held/unheld stays encoded by tile colour; the panel
  carries all detail)." Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-05. Research:
  confirmed current tiles print the full `intel.label` at 7px in
  `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` `renderHexTile`.
- Q2: "How is a hex 'selected' to populate the detail panel?" — Answer
  (operator, interactive reply): "(a) The focused hex (keyboard tab/arrows
  already move focus; pointer-over can also drive it; click still deploys)."
  Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-05.

---

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2** – Hex map scene with known-ahead intel (completed)
- **AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU** – Make Phase Shift and wormhole-emergence effects unmistakable (completed)
- **AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP** – Between-sortie defence report and attract-mode traversal (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: aggression, details, far, full, hex, hexmap, level, map, panel, read, selected, show, shows, small, text
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: aggression, details, far, full, hex, hexmap, level, map, panel, read, selected, show, shows, small, text
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: far, full, hex, level, map, panel, read, selected, show, shows, small, text, unreadable
